cyclical.reason: Subscription revenue under multi-year contracts (renewal rate 98%, RPO 29.7B) and growth of 21-30% every year FY2021-FY2025, including 2022; no cycle in the history.

bear.reason_he: התשואה על ההון של החברה הייתה כ-14% בשנה האחרונה וכ-9% בממוצע (רווח תפעולי חשבונאי, כולל מוניטין). אם הרכישות של 2025-2026 (כ-11.2 מיליארד דולר, ממומנות בחלקן בחוב) לא מרוויחות והרווחיות החשבונאית נשארת ב-10% כפי שהונחה ל-2026, כל דולר של צמיחה עולה הרבה הון - ולכן מכפיל נמוך, עדיין מעל מחיר ההון.

base.reason_he: ב-2022-2025 הרווח התפעולי אחרי מס עלה בכ-1.16 מיליארד דולר מול תוספת הון של כ-5.9 מיליארד - כ-20%; החישוב של המנוע לתשואה על ההון הנוסף (3 שנים) נותן 26.2%. הצמיחה האורגנית כמעט לא דורשת הון (השקעות כ-6.5% מההכנסות), אבל הרכישות של כ-11 מיליארד מדללות את התשואה; לכן 22%, בין 20% ל-26%, קרוב לצד הנמוך. אותו מספר משמש גם בהערכת התזרים.

bull.reason_he: אם יעד ה-AI (ACV של 1.7 מיליארד דולר ל-2026, הועלה מ-1 מיליארד), הצריכה של סוכני AI (פי 13 השנה) והגידול בלקוחות הגדולים (680 מעל 5 מיליון דולר, מ-553) ממשיכים, והרכישות מתחילות להרוויח - הצמיחה נשארת סביב 20% כמעט בלי הון נוסף והתשואה על ההון החדש קרובה לזו של המנוע האורגני. זה עוד לא הוכח בדוחות.

bear.event_he: צמיחת ההתחייבויות לשנה הקרובה (cRPO) יורדת מ-21% ל-18.5% ברבעון הרביעי, וחלק מהקצב הנוכחי נקנה ברכישות; ההאטה האורגנית ממשיכה ב-2027.
שותף ערוץ פדרלי אחד הוא 12% מההכנסות ו-20% מהחייבים, וחקירת משרד המשפטים עדיין פתוחה; פגיעה בתקציבי הממשל האמריקאי מורידה צמיחה.
רכישות של כ-11.2 מיליארד דולר (Armis, Veza, Moveworks) מעלות את החוב ל-7.5 מיליארד ואת הפחתות הנכסים; הרווח החשבונאי ירד ל-9.5% מההכנסות ברבעון.
סוכני AI מצמצמים את מספר המושבים שלקוחות קונים ומתחרים כמו מיקרוסופט וסיילספורס לוחצים על המחיר.

base.event_he: הכנסות המנויים ל-2026 מגיעות לכ-15.8 מיליארד דולר, מעט מעל התחזית כמו בכל שבעת הרבעונים האחרונים.
ב-2027 ההכנסות צומחות בערך בקצב ההתחייבויות החוזיות לשנה הקרובה (כ-19%), עם שימור לקוחות של 98%.
שיעור הרווח התפעולי (ללא תגמול במניות) נשאר סביב 31.5%-32% ותזרים המזומנים החופשי כ-36% מההכנסות.
מכירות ה-AI מגיעות ליעד של 1.7 מיליארד דולר בשנה עד סוף 2026.

bull.event_he: ההנהלה אומרת שההאצה האמיתית מה-AI תגיע ב-2027: מכירות ה-AI עוברות את 1.7 מיליארד, צריכת סוכנים ממשיכה לגדול (פי 13 השנה), והצמיחה עולה מעל 21%.
העסקאות הגדולות ממשיכות להאיץ: 19 עסקאות מעל 5 מיליון דולר ברבעון (+135%) ו-680 לקוחות מעל 5 מיליון דולר בשנה (+23%).
האבטחה (Armis ו-Veza) והשירות האוטונומי (Moveworks, 100 מיליון דולר בשלושה רבעונים) הופכים למנועי צמיחה נוספים.
השימוש הפנימי ב-AI מוריד עלויות ומעלה את הרווחיות לכיוון יעד 'כלל 60'.

key_risk.reading_he: הצמיחה האורגנית מאטה: ההתחייבויות לשנה הקרובה צפויות לצמוח רק 18.5% ברבעון הרביעי לעומת 21%, חלק מהקצב בא מרכישות, ובמקביל תגמול במניות של כ-15% מההכנסות והפחתות הרכישות שומרים את הרווח החשבונאי נמוך (9.5% ברבעון).

bottleneck.reading_he: NOW claims to supply governed workflow execution across disparate systems of record, a need it says AI intensifies (management positioning in the 10-K). The 10-K itself describes a fragmented market with low barriers to entry and warns that system-of-record owners may block NOW's access to their data, so NOW is not a capacity bottleneck in the semiconductor sense: its scarcity is installed workflow depth (98% renewal rate) rather than a resource others cannot add. How long enterprises lack governed AI-workflow platforms, and how fast Salesforce, Microsoft, Workday, Oracle and SAP close it by embedding agents, is not evidenced (hypothesis).

future.reading_he: Enterprise buyers are paying more for NOW's workflow and AI layer, measured in NOW's own numbers: customers above $5M ACV 680 vs 553 a year earlier (+23%), 19 deals above $5M net new ACV in Q3 2026 (+135% y/y), RPO $29.7bn (+22%) and cRPO $13.65bn (+20.5% reported, includes Armis and Moveworks), AI ACV target raised from $1.0bn to $1.7bn for end-2026 (management target, not a fact) and agentic AI consumption up 13x year to date. No independent market-size study (Gartner/IDC) was retrieved, so the direction of the whole market beyond NOW's own demand is not evidenced; management itself expects its growth rate to decline over the long term.

moat.note: Evidenced moat source is switching costs on the installed workflow base (98% renewal) plus faster growth than Salesforce and Workday; but GAAP ROIC was about 14% last year and about 9% on average against an 8% reference, close to the cost of capital once stock compensation is counted, the 10-K describes low barriers to entry, and goodwill rose to about $10bn in 2026, which will weigh on returns on capital. Strong cash economics (FCF margin above 30% for six years) do not yet show up as high GAAP returns.

switching_costs.note: 98% renewal rate, RPO $29.7bn with average contract duration lengthening per the CFO; workflows embedded across IT, HR and customer service are costly to replace versus Microsoft or Salesforce alternatives.

retention.note: Renewal rate 98%; customers above $5M ACV grew 23% y/y. Net revenue retention is not disclosed (gap).

pricing_power.note: Customers accept hybrid seat plus consumption pricing for AI (CFO); but the FY2026 non-GAAP subscription gross margin guide slipped from 81.5% to 81%, and delivery services for large AI deals are given at a gross loss (professional services gross profit -$39M in Q3), a concession to win AI deals.

customer_concentration.note: One U.S. federal channel partner and systems integrator is 12% of revenue (11% in FY2025) and 20% of receivables; it is a channel for many agencies rather than one end buyer, but it ties a large slice to U.S. federal procurement.

competition.note: NOW out-grows each named competitor (Salesforce, Workday, Microsoft, Oracle) on whole-company numbers, but all of them are embedding AI agents in their own systems of record and Microsoft is far larger and more profitable; the 10-K calls the market fragmented with low barriers to entry.

substitutes.note: AI agents shrinking ticket-handling headcount is a real substitution risk to seat revenue (opinion, unsized); NOW's own agentic consumption grew 13x year to date and pricing is hybrid, so far evidence that NOW captures the agent layer rather than being replaced by it.

management.note: Subscription revenue beat the guided midpoint in all 7 quarters read (+0.3% to +2.7%) and the AI ACV target was raised twice in 2026; management also states plainly that growth will decline over the long term.

capital_allocation.note: About $11.2bn spent on Moveworks, Veza and Armis in ten months, funded partly with debt (carrying debt about $7.5bn from about $1.5bn); returns on these acquisitions are not yet evidenced and the organic growth rate is not disclosed. Buybacks of $2.2bn in 9M 2026 roughly offset stock compensation of $1.8bn (quarterly SBC $630M vs $492M a year earlier, +28%), so share count is flat (1.043bn Q3, 1.05bn guided for Q4) rather than falling.

governance.note: Open DOJ investigation into the 2023 hiring of the former U.S. Army CIO (President and COO resigned July 2024); timing and outcome cannot be predicted per the 10-Q.

regulation.note: Government procurement rules and possible debarment matter because a federal channel partner is 12% of revenue; data-residency and AI rules are generic risk factors, unsized.

technology_ai.note: Paid AI adoption shows in NOW's own numbers: AI net new ACV +65% y/y in Q3, AI deals above $1M up 4.5x, agentic consumption up 13x year to date, AI ACV target $1.7bn for end-2026 (management-defined metric, target not yet reported as achieved).

geopolitics.note: About 63% of 9M 2026 revenue from North America (about 60% U.S.), EMEA 25%, APAC 12%, no China breakout; sanctions and tariffs are generic 10-K risks with no revenue sized; a software subscription business with limited hardware exposure.

market_direction.reading: Enterprise buyers are paying more for NOW's workflow and AI layer, measured in NOW's own numbers: customers above $5M ACV 680 vs 553 a year earlier (+23%), 19 deals above $5M net new ACV in Q3 2026 (+135% y/y), RPO $29.7bn (+22%) and cRPO $13.65bn (+20.5% reported, includes Armis and Moveworks), AI ACV target raised from $1.0bn to $1.7bn for end-2026 (management target, not a fact) and agentic AI consumption up 13x year to date. No independent market-size study (Gartner/IDC) was retrieved, so the direction of the whole market beyond NOW's own demand is not evidenced; management itself expects its growth rate to decline over the long term.

bottleneck_potential.reading: NOW claims to supply governed workflow execution across disparate systems of record, a need it says AI intensifies (management positioning in the 10-K). The 10-K itself describes a fragmented market with low barriers to entry and warns that system-of-record owners may block NOW's access to their data, so NOW is not a capacity bottleneck in the semiconductor sense: its scarcity is installed workflow depth (98% renewal rate) rather than a resource others cannot add. How long enterprises lack governed AI-workflow platforms, and how fast Salesforce, Microsoft, Workday, Oracle and SAP close it by embedding agents, is not evidenced (hypothesis).

share_trajectory.reading: On whole-company growth from each company's own filings, NOW (+20.9% FY2025, +20.5% Q3 2026) grew faster than every named competitor: Salesforce +9.6% (FY Jan-2026), Workday +13.1% (FY Jan-2026), Microsoft +17.8% and Oracle +17.4% (whole company, including cloud infrastructure). This suggests NOW is gaining share against Salesforce and Workday in the overlapping workflow budgets, but segment-level share (Service Cloud, Dynamics, Workday HCM service) was not retrieved, and NOW's 2026 growth includes acquired revenue (Moveworks, Veza, Armis) with no organic rate disclosed, so the share gain is directional, not measured.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than Salesforce and Workday on growth (about 2x Salesforce's rate, 1.6x Workday's) with similar gross margin to Salesforce (77.5% vs 77.7%) and higher GAAP operating margin than Workday (13.7% vs 7.5%), but below Salesforce (20.1%) and far below Microsoft (46.8%) and Oracle (30.6%) on GAAP operating margin. Microsoft is the strongest named rival: far larger, owns Copilot and the Power Platform and is also a distribution partner. NOW's advantages shown in its own data are retention (98% renewal), large-customer expansion (+23% $5M customers) and a seven-for-seven record of beating its subscription guidance; its weakness is a lower GAAP margin after stock compensation (15.5% of Q3 revenue) and acquisition amortization.

threats.reading: Substitution: AI agents could reduce the number of employees handling IT tickets and so the seats NOW charges for (investor worry cited in press, opinion; NOW's answer is hybrid seat plus consumption pricing, which customers accept per the CFO). In-sourcing and new entrants: the 10-K names custom in-house builds, point and platform AI solutions and systems integrators, in a market with low barriers to entry. Systems-of-record owners (Salesforce, Microsoft, Workday, Oracle, SAP) may restrict data access. Regulation and government: a U.S. federal channel partner is 12% of revenue and 20% of receivables, and a DOJ investigation into the 2023 hire of the Army CIO is open with an unpredictable outcome. Deceleration: Q4 cRPO growth guided down to 18.5% cc from 21%.

bottlenecks.reading: NOW states in its 10-K Item 1 that enterprises need a layer that unifies disparate systems, enforces business logic and governance and executes workflows, and that AI has intensified rather than removed that need; the scarce thing NOW claims to supply is governed workflow execution across silos. This is management's own positioning, not independent evidence.

Paid AI adoption in NOW's own numbers: management raised its 2026 AI annual contract value target to $1.7bn (up 70% from the start of the year) and RPO is 29.7bn (+22%), cRPO 13.65bn (+20.5%) at Q3 2026. AI ACV is a management-defined target, to be checked by the documents lane against the call.

Capacity and duration of the shortage not evidenced by an independent source (no Gartner/IDC/regulator data retrieved): how long enterprises lack governed AI-workflow platforms, and who adds capacity (system-of-record vendors Salesforce, Microsoft, Workday, Oracle, SAP embedding agents; in-house builds; point-solution startups), is a hypothesis.

Risk to the bottleneck: the 10-K warns that systems-of-record operators may build mechanisms that prevent NOW's solutions from accessing their data, and that competitors may incorporate AI faster; low barriers to entry per Item 1 mean the moat is workflow depth and installed base, not scarcity of technology.
